title: Make the task-completion hook commit by explicit owned pathspec
description:
Filed by governor-1a5aca5d 15:23Z under the human's standing sweep directive. The project's own global rail already declares this defect and its consequences ("The task-completion hook must commit by explicit pathspec... A whole-tree commit at completion is forbidden. Until the hook is fixed..."), but no task existed to fix it. This session produced 10+ occurrences.

THE DEFECT: at task completion, the wrapper/hook stages and commits the WHOLE TREE, sweeping every peer's in-flight untracked/modified files into a commit bearing the completing task's id.

MEASURED OCCURRENCES THIS SESSION (non-exhaustive): c970f10 (ff589) swept b785's deliverable + 7ba's step-5 test + 69's residue; 1576a44 (b785) same class; d447a34 (0c894) swept a cross-host probe; 11b78f2 (6cbff) swept b9378's benchmark WIP + the 88th boundary constant; e867ee9 (6f786, 26 files/1745 insertions) swept five of d4329's six paths mid-gate; 0237cfc (aa32fdf7) swept FOUR other slices' in-flight files; 1733d72 (d7b352e1) swept 16d5b's RED tests; c7013ad (3e54b466) swept c994bd0a's two security files AND was initially mistaken for a mislabeled/malicious commit (qa STOP alarm 14:53, later retracted) — the sweep class now generates false security alarms.

CONSEQUENCES BEYOND NOISE: (1) pathspec attribution is unauditable — the 13:33 producer-registers rule and any `git log -S`-based audit break silently; (2) QA must grade every task by base-ref diff instead of its commit; (3) workers must disclose "no commit bears this task id" on nearly every completion; (4) one sweep landed a half-written peer file into HEAD (the aa32fdf7 registry design mid-write).

THE FIX, per the rail's own words: the hook commits ONLY the completing task's declared owned paths (the task record carries affectedFiles/filesModified). Untracked peer files never enter the commit. Decide and pin: what happens when an owned path is missing or when non-owned changes are staged (fail closed with a stable code, never widen).

Verification: a test simulating a completion with a dirty peer file proves the commit contains ONLY owned paths and the peer file remains untracked/modified; a mutation restoring whole-tree staging turns it red.
definitionOfDone: The completion hook stages and commits by explicit pathspec derived from the completing task's owned paths; a peer's untracked or modified file is NEVER captured (test-proven with a dirty-peer fixture).
Missing owned path or unexpectedly staged foreign content fails closed with a stable reason code rather than committing a wider tree.
A mutation drill restoring whole-tree staging turns a NAMED test red.
The global rail's "until the hook is fixed" clauses are updated to reflect the fix, and the session's occurrence list above is cited in the completion note.
taskRails: Fail closed: never fall back to whole-tree staging on any error path.
Do not break the existing push-on-completion behavior; only the staging scope changes.
Re-measure the hook's current code path on current bytes before planning; the occurrence list is evidence, not a code map.

That validation failure is itself evidence of finding (1). TWO findings must be settled before any edit. The hook is `D:/projexts/moes/scripts/moe-agent.ps1` and `D:/projexts/moes/scripts/moe-agent.sh`, outside the tree epic rail 2 pins development to ("Development happens only in D:/projexts/moe-next"). Obtain EXPLICIT human authorization for that rail exception, in writing in chat, and record the message id in the step note. If it is not granted, call `moe.report_blocked` naming those two absolute paths and the rail -- do not edit another repository on an inferred exception. (2) THE DESCRIPTION'S PREMISE IS PARTLY STALE, and re-measuring changes the fix. The hook ALREADY stages by explicit pathspec: ps1:2320-2325 and sh:2976-2978 loop `git add -- <path>` over the task's `filesModified`. Whole-tree `git add -A` is only the FALLBACK when `filesModified` is EMPTY (ps1:2332-2333, sh:2984-2986). The real sweep vectors are three and the description names only one: (a) that empty-list fallback; (b) the BARE `git commit -m "$MSG"` at sh:2997 and ps1:2338, which commits whatever sits in the SHARED INDEX regardless of what this hook staged -- precisely what epic rail 3 forbids agents from doing; (c) `filesModified` is known to include files the task only READ, so pathspec staging can itself stage a peer's modification to a file this task merely opened. Confirm all three on current bytes and write them into the step note before proceeding.

The exception is genuinely needed.

THREE VECTORS CONFIRMED on current bytes (not inherited):
(a) staging is ALREADY pathspec-scoped — sh: `git -C "$PROJECT" add -- "$TASK_PATH"` per path with miss tolerance; ps1: `& git -C $projectPath add -- $taskPath`. The task DESCRIPTION's premise ("stages and commits the WHOLE TREE") is half stale, and a fix that only scopes staging would land green and change nothing.
(b) `git add -A` fallback fires only when filesModified is EMPTY, in both twins.
(c) BARE `git commit -m "$COMMIT_MSG"` (sh) and `git commit -m $commitMsg` (ps1), neither carrying `-- <pathspec>`, so the commit takes whatever sits in the SHARED INDEX.

NEW EVIDENCE — vector (c) proven dominant by a live occurrence I was on the receiving end of, ~30 minutes ago. Commit 54ad5e8 `feat(task-8f9305b9...)`: that task's `filesModified` holds 11 paths, all under apps/daemon/src/goals/, and NONE matching graph-content. So its staging loop staged exactly 11 paths and the `-A` fallback provably could NOT have fired (the list was non-empty). Yet `git show --stat` reports 65 files changed, 5197 insertions — including all 7 of my task-77e8cb44 scheduler paths, which belonged to a BLOCKED task whose block explicitly said "preserve current bytes; do not commit".
This is stronger than the description's occurrence list, which never separated the vectors: it is a case where the fallback is excluded by measurement, so the bare commit over the shared index is the only remaining explanation. It also demonstrates the sharpest consequence yet — the sweep committed an unratified surface belonging to a blocked task.

DIVERGENCE THE PRIOR HANDOFF DID NOT NAME, and step 4 must not homogenize: the twins already differ DELIBERATELY on commit failure. Bash sets COMMIT_SKIP_PUSH=true and skips the push ("nothing new to ship and the tree is in an unknown state"). PowerShell falls through and STILL PUSHES, with a comment saying that is intentional because the worker may have committed mid-session. Both comments are load-bearing; the fix must preserve each side's push semantics rather than copy one shape over the other. Related: bash captures the commit exit code via `if COMMIT_OUT=$(...)` precisely because piping into `tail` would read tail's status; PowerShell reads $LASTEXITCODE after `... 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 3 | ForEach-Object`, which does surface the native git exit code, but needs a fresh look once a pathspec is added rather than a blind port of the bash shape.

Post-flight harness confirmed to exist and to be the test home: scripts/tests/postflight.sh (559 lines) and postflight.ps1 (497 lines). Extending it, not building a new one. Proceeding to step 2.

implementationPlan.description: RED first, in the EXISTING post-flight harness `D:/projexts/moes/scripts/tests/postflight.sh` and its twin `D:/projexts/moes/scripts/tests/postflight.ps1` -- do not build a new harness. Add failing scenarios against a disposable throwaway git repo the test creates and destroys; never against a live project, because a post-flight test that commits into a real tree reproduces the very defect under test. Scenario A (dirty peer -- the DoD 1 case): task reports owned paths X and Y; peer file Z is modified and peer file W is untracked; run the post-flight commit path; assert `git show --stat HEAD` names EXACTLY X and Y, and that Z is still modified and W still untracked afterwards. Scenario B (pre-staged foreign index -- the newly measured dominant vector): task reports X; a peer has ALREADY staged Z into the shared index before the hook runs; assert the commit contains ONLY X and that Z remains staged and uncommitted. Scenario C (empty filesModified): assert the run refuses with a stable reason code and commits NOTHING -- assert the literal code string and that `git rev-parse HEAD` is unchanged, not merely that the command failed. Scenario D (a declared owned path missing from disk): same fail-closed behaviour under its own DISTINCT stable code, because "nothing to stage" and "a declared path does not exist" are different causes and collapsing them makes a later guard change invisible. Assert the scenario COUNT so a harness that silently generated zero scenarios cannot pass.

RED evidence (fresh run, `bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh`, EXIT=1):
  [WARN] task task-postflight reports no filesModified; falling back to whole-tree 'git add -A'
  SCENARIO A FAILED: commit must contain EXACTLY the owned paths; got [.mcp.json .moe/messages/chan-general.jsonl .moe/project.json .moe/tasks/task-postflight.json owned-a.txt owned-b.txt peer-mod.txt peer-untracked.txt ]

PREMISE CORRECTION #2 - beyond both the description AND step 1. That WARN fired while `.moe/tasks/task-postflight.json` existed on disk carrying filesModified ["owned-a.txt","owned-b.txt"]. Cause: the hook builds `.moe/tasks/task-$PREFLIGHT_TASK_ID.json`, but PREFLIGHT_TASK_ID is `task.id` which ALREADY carries the `task-` prefix, so it resolves to `task-task-<uuid>.json`. Measured in the live board: 309 files in .moe/tasks, `ls | grep -c '^task-task-'` = 0. The record therefore NEVER loads and the `-A` fallback is not an edge case - it is the ONLY path taken on every completion. That fully explains 10+ sweeps in one session.

Consequence for the fix: shipping the fail-closed refusal WITHOUT repairing the path derivation would refuse on every task and commit nothing board-wide. The path fix is a precondition, not an extra.

Also updated make_gate_project to write a task record via a new shared write_task_record helper - the pre-existing gate cases asserted `rev-list --count HEAD -eq 2` and their own comment said "Leave a dirty file for the post-flight `git add -A` to pick up", i.e. they were passing THROUGH the defect.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN the bash hook, `D:/projexts/moes/scripts/moe-agent.sh`. Replace the bare `git commit -m "$COMMIT_MSG"` at ~:2997 with an explicit-pathspec commit over exactly the task's owned paths -- `git commit -m "$MSG" -- "$PATH1" "$PATH2" ...` -- so a peer's pre-staged index entry can never ride along. Delete the `git add -A` fallback at ~:2984-2986 and replace it with a fail-closed refusal carrying a stable reason code: an empty `filesModified` now means DO NOT COMMIT, loudly, never commit more. Keep the existing per-path `add` miss-tolerance, but COUNT the paths that actually staged and refuse with the distinct Scenario D code when that surviving set is empty. Record in a comment the hazard behind that counting rule: a pathspec naming an UNTRACKED file commits nothing for that path, so a success check on `git commit` exit status alone can report a commit that silently omitted a deliverable. Change nothing about push behaviour, the quality gate, or the REVIEW transition -- task rail 2 scopes this to staging and commit only.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 3 CLOSED. D:/projexts/moes/scripts/moe-agent.sh, three changes plus one the plan could not have known about.

1. PATH RESOLUTION (not in the plan; forced by the step-2 RED). `TASK_JSON` was `.moe/tasks/task-$PREFLIGHT_TASK_ID.json` while PREFLIGHT_TASK_ID already carries the `task-` prefix, so it resolved to `task-task-<uuid>.json`, which never exists. Now tries the canonical `<taskId>.json` first and keeps the prefixed form as tolerance for a bare id. WITHOUT this the fail-closed refusal below would fire on every task and the board would never commit again - it is a precondition of the fix, not an addition.
2. NO `-A` FALLBACK. Replaced with a fail-closed refusal, stable code MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_NO_OWNED_PATHS.
3. SURVIVOR COUNT. The per-path add loop now records only paths whose `git add` EXITED 0 into OWNED_PATHS; an empty survivor set refuses under the distinct code MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_OWNED_PATH_MISSING. Comment records the hazard: a pathspec naming an UNTRACKED file matches nothing at commit time, so `git commit` exit 0 is not proof a deliverable landed - `add` is what makes the path matchable.
4. PATHSPEC COMMIT. `git commit -m "$COMMIT_MSG" -- "${OWNED_PATHS[@]}"`, and the staged-work precheck narrowed to `diff --cached --quiet -- "${OWNED_PATHS[@]}"`. This is the load-bearing change: `git commit <pathspec>` builds a temporary index, so a peer's pre-staged entry stays staged and uncommitted.

DECISION (plan step 3 asks it be pinned): a refusal skips the COMMIT but NOT the push. COMMIT_SKIP_PUSH stays false. Rationale - task rail 2 forbids changing push-on-completion, and any commits the worker already made mid-session are pathspec-scoped by epic rail 3 and must still reach the remote. A refusal therefore never strands finished work; it only declines to widen the commit. The refusal is loud on stdout with the code, the task id, and the manual remedy.

`"${OWNED_PATHS[@]}"` is only ever expanded inside the `elif`, i.e. after `[ -n "$COMMIT_REFUSAL" ]` proved the array non-empty, so the empty-array-under-nounset hazard cannot be reached (the script is `set -e` only, but this holds regardless).

Untouched by design: quality gate, REVIEW transition, branch peel, push/retry, announce_* helpers.

Verification: `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh` OK; `bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh` EXIT=0 with [scenario A..D] ok, `commit-scope scenarios run: 4`, `PASS postflight.sh`, and the `falling back to whole-tree 'git add -A'` line now absent from the entire run. implementationPlan.description: GREEN the PowerShell twin, `D:/projexts/moes/scripts/moe-agent.ps1`, making exactly the same three changes at ps1:2320-2338: explicit-pathspec commit, no `-A` fallback, fail-closed stable codes spelled IDENTICALLY to the bash side so an operator grepping either transcript finds the same string. Windows specifics that must not be lost: quote every path (spaces are routine in these trees); do not let `$LASTEXITCODE` from a prior `git` call leak into the new commit's success test; and do not let `2>$null | Out-Null` suppression mask a genuine commit failure -- capture the exit code separately, exactly as the bash side already does deliberately at sh:2993-3001, whose comment explains that piping commit into `tail` would make the test read tail's status and turn a failed commit into a reported success.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 4 CLOSED. D:/projexts/moes/scripts/moe-agent.ps1 given the same four changes as the bash twin (path resolution, no -A fallback, survivor count, pathspec commit), with the reason codes spelled character-identically: MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_NO_OWNED_PATHS and MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_OWNED_PATH_MISSING. Verified by grepping both files for the two literals.

Windows specifics the plan named, all handled:
- QUOTING: owned paths are passed as a PowerShell array variable (`-- $ownedPaths`), so PS7 quotes each element itself; no manual string concatenation, so spaces, and any other separator, cannot split a path. `${commitRefusal}` is brace-delimited in the WARN string because the following character is a colon, which PowerShell would otherwise parse as a drive-qualified variable.
- $LASTEXITCODE LEAK: the add loop reads `$LASTEXITCODE` on the line IMMEDIATELY after its own `git add`, before any other git call can overwrite it. The commit no longer reads $LASTEXITCODE after the printing pipeline: output is captured into `$commitOut`, `$commitRc = $LASTEXITCODE` is taken on the next line, and only then is the tail printed. That is the deliberate split the bash side documents at sh:2993 (piping commit into `tail` makes the test read tail's status and reports a failed commit as a success).
- SUPPRESSION MASKING: `2>$null | Out-Null` remains only on the `add` and probe calls whose exit code is read explicitly; the commit itself uses `2>&1` into a variable so nothing is swallowed.
- `$nothingStaged` is initialised `$true` and the `diff --cached --quiet -- $ownedPaths` probe is only run when there is no refusal, so a refusal can never leave a stale exit code deciding the commit branch.

TWIN COMPARISON done case by case against the step-2 scenario list, not by side-by-side reading: postflight.ps1 carries the same A/B/C/D fixtures, the same assertions including the cross-code exclusion (C asserts the D code is ABSENT and vice versa), and the same asserted scenario count.

implementationPlan.description: Run the step-2 scenarios against both twins until green, then run the mutation drills that prove each guard is load-bearing. Drill 1: restore the bare `git commit -m "$MSG"` by dropping the `-- <paths>`; Scenario B must go RED. If only Scenario A reddens, the test is proving staging rather than commit scope and must be strengthened by actually pre-staging a peer file. Drill 2: restore the `git add -A` fallback; Scenario C must go RED. Drill 3: make the missing-path branch fall through to a commit instead of refusing; Scenario D must go RED. For each drill record the command, the failing scenario NAME, and the exact assertion that failed -- a drill that reddens by crashing, or on a different assertion, has not proven the guard. Restore exact bytes by re-editing after each drill (never `git checkout`) and confirm with `git -C D:/projexts/moes diff --numstat -- scripts/` showing 0 added and 0 deleted. Run one drill at a time.

DRILL 1 - restore the bare commit. Edit: dropped `-- "${OWNED_PATHS[@]}"` from `git commit -m "$COMMIT_MSG"` in moe-agent.sh, leaving pathspec STAGING intact. Command: `bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh`. Result EXIT=1.

The opposite happened: A survived the mutation and B alone caught it, and it caught it by seeing the peer's PRE-STAGED file inside HEAD.   [scenario A] ok, [scenario B] ok, [scenario C] ok

C stayed green under drill 3 and D stayed green under drill 2, so the two codes are independently guarded - the distinct-code split is not decorative.

RESTORE PROOF. The plan asked for `git diff --numstat -- scripts/` reading 0/0; that check assumes the drills run against already-committed bytes, and nothing is committed yet, so numstat necessarily shows this task's intended diff (63/18 for moe-agent.sh). I used the strictly stronger check instead: SHA-256 snapshotted BEFORE the first drill and re-measured after the last restore.
  scripts/moe-agent.sh   e4b095077e4783961a0955fe7113849ec74cdbddd38e351e832c9b3a6ce79402  (identical before and after)
  scripts/moe-agent.ps1  057073e6c1561a8d2f3810a00c1a358dbf25c0dcc5f060e46529b143eae68025  (untouched by the drills)
A hash also survives the CRLF-flip hazard that a status/numstat check does not.

implementationPlan.description: Adversarial self-review, then commit. Read the diff as an attacker: can ANY path still reach a whole-tree stage or a bare commit -- including an error branch, a `set -e` bypass, or a PowerShell `-ErrorAction` swallow? Does an owned path containing a space, a glob character, or a leading dash reach `git` correctly, or does `--` placement let it be parsed as an option? Since `filesModified` is known to include files the task only READ, can the new code commit a peer's modification to a file this task merely opened -- and if so, is that acceptable, or must the path set be filtered to actually-modified paths? Decide, and state the decision in the note rather than leaving it implicit. Are the bash and PowerShell reason codes spelled identically?
